lines: I do not have a trade for it yet, but coming home safely feels like honest work.
Home again, whole enough to <gold><pulse>thank you</pulse></gold> properly. That matters.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I will count that as good work.
I never thought the village bell could sound that welcoming.
Thanks for matching my pace when the road got rough.
I was running out of food before I was ready to admit it.
Seeing the first roof over the hill took the weight right off me.
I learned more about the road than I did about choosing a trade.
Next time I will pack better, but I would follow that route again.
You got us home without making a show of it. I respect that.
The last stretch felt twice as long as the rest of the trip.
I am glad we shared what food we had instead of pretending there was plenty.
My feet are sore, but nothing else is broken. Good enough for me.
I kept track of every turn on the way back. I think I could find it again.
Coming through the gate felt better than finishing any errand.
I was worried the road would outlast our supplies. It nearly did.
Nobody had to carry me home, so I am calling the trip a success.
I understand now why people look back when the village disappears from sight.
Give me a night to rest and I might even remember the good parts.
We left together and came back together. That is what matters.
I was looking for direction, not bruises. Still, I made it back.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
Every step pulled at the wound by the end.
I was trying so hard not to slow everyone down.
The first doorway inside the village looked like a palace.
Thanks for keeping pace when I could not.
I should have packed bandages before extra food.
The blood dried before the road ended. I did not like that.
Home felt farther away every time I looked up.
The neighbors helped me through the gate without asking questions.
I am sore, angry, and very glad to be back.
Getting home was the only job that mattered by then.
I kept saying I was fine because stopping felt worse.
The road did not beat me, but it came close.
Give me time to heal before anyone calls this a success.
I learned where every loose stone was on that last stretch.
Next time I speak up before the pain gets that bad.
I did not need heroics. I needed a steady arm.
We came back injured, but we came back together.
I followed because I thought you knew where we were going. I was wrong about more than the road.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
I keep wondering when the plan changed.
The walk home felt longer after I stopped trusting you.
I watched the path while the danger walked beside me.
Do not ask me to forget just because the bruise faded.
I believed your directions. That is what you used against me.
The silence after the attack said more than your excuses do.
Next time I ask where we are going before I take one step.
I made it home, but I left my trust on that road.
You became the threat before I understood what was happening.
I will listen to an apology. I will not pretend it fixes everything.
The worst blow came from knowing who struck it.
I should not have needed to guard myself from the person leading.
If we travel again, you stay where I can see you.
I do not know whether the destination was ever real.
You turned a simple journey into a warning I will remember.
Trust comes back slower than footsteps.
We can talk about the road when you are ready to tell the truth.
I learned I am not ready for a career in boating, but I survived the lesson.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding whether the rest of the plan did.
Water carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
I have never been so happy to stand on ordinary dirt.
Next time I am bringing dry food and sitting where you tell me.
The village looked very small from the water and very good on the way back.
I finally understand why everyone checks a boat before climbing into it.
My legs still feel like the ground is moving.
Thanks for not laughing when I grabbed the side with both hands.
I thought being useful meant helping. In that boat, it meant keeping still.
The current had more say in our route than either of us did.
I will remember that knocking under the hull for a while.
We made it back with the boat upright. That is a respectable result.
I should have asked how far we were going before we pushed off.
There was nowhere to stretch and nowhere to hide from the water.
I spent half the trip watching the shore and the other half missing it.
If we do that again, I want the seat farthest from the edge.
I did not enjoy the deep water, but I trusted you to get us across it.
The first step onto land nearly made me laugh.
I am glad we went. I am even happier that we are done.
